statement: A pilot can record a versioned migration plan, complete an initial load, keep a bounded change feed or dual-write adapter until a declared high-water mark, run parity checks, switch selected traffic, and roll back while producing durable receipts for source position, target state, outstanding divergence, and the exact cutover decision; no step infers success from process exit or a disconnected client. Verified at HEAD 761dc17c7: no migration-plan, cutover, or receipt machinery exists (docs/migration.md documents the absence); this Quest builds the general receipt/workflow owner in the AGPL repo and keeps source-specific PostgreSQL CDC integration in an external adapter, with that boundary explicit.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn an independent verifier before audit and handoff and record its stable evidence id.

One general receipt/workflow owner records plans, positions, parity, and decisions in this repo; source-specific PostgreSQL CDC integration stays in an external adapter. No second migration-state store.

Every step (initial load, change feed, parity, cutover, rollback) produces a durable receipt naming source position, target state, outstanding divergence, and the exact decision; success is never inferred from process exit or a disconnected client.
Required failure cases: source reconnect, duplicate change, out-of-order change, target outage, schema drift, cutover timeout, parity mismatch, and rollback after partial traffic.
Removing receipt durability, parity checks, or divergence accounting must make cutover and rollback scenarios fail closed rather than silently proceed.
